messages:
alex: Hey @support — customer running Private agent in their VPC reports installer fails when pulling Python wheels and model shards. Error shows TLS handshake failure and sometimes DNS NXDOMAIN for model-registry.redwood.internal :thinking_face:

support-customer: repro steps I ran: fresh k8s nodes, cluster NAT, outbound only via corporate proxy. Installer logs: `curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure` and `getaddrinfo: Name or service not known` for model-registry host.

sophia: do they use TLS interception / proxy with MITM? those handshake errors + OCSP failing usually point to TLS proxy dropping SNI or re-signing certs. any proxy IPs or TLS decrypt on path?

support-customer: yes they have an outbound TLS intercepting proxy at boundary, but they say they allow passthrough for some hosts. they asked which FQDNs we need whitelisted.

alex: quick ask: can you paste the `curl -v` output from the agent node (obfuscate any tokens)? Example we want to see `Server certificate` and `subjectAltName` errors. sample command we used:```curl -v --connect-timeout 10 https://model-registry.redwood-internal/health || true```

support-customer: pasted logs: ```* Connected to model-registry.redwood-internal (10.10.8.5) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* Server certificate: CN=registry.internal
* subjectAltName does not match model-registry.redwood-internal
* SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name mismatch```

mike: looks like internal load-balancer is serving cert for `registry.internal` while SNI the client sends includes `model-registry.redwood-internal`. Probably they have internal split-horizon DNS or hostname rewrite on proxy.

sophia: other things to whitelist for installer: pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, deb.nodesource.com, apt.pkg.redwood.ai (our apt mirror), telemetry.redwood.ai, oauth.redwood.ai, registry.redwood-internal (model shards + kv), cdn.fastly.net (model shard CDN), and ocsp.digicert.com/ocsp.* for cert stapling/OCSP checks. also allow outbound to object stores like s3.amazonaws.com and us-west-2.amazonaws.com for model pulls.

support-customer: can you give exact FQDN list and whether we need IP ranges? we can only allow specific FQDNs in proxy rules; security requires IP ranges for firewall.

alex: suggested allowlist (please confirm with security):
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- packages.redwood.ai (apt/deb)
- telemetry.redwood.ai (443, 443/tls, port 443 only)
- oauth.redwood.ai (token endpoints)
- registry.redwood-internal (model metadata + auth)
- shard-*.model-cdn.redwood.ai (wildcard for model shards)
- cdn.fastly.net (for shard redirects)
- s3.amazonaws.com, *.s3.amazonaws.com (for presigned URLs)
- ocsp.digicert.com, crl3.digicert.com (OCSP/CRL checks)

sophia: about IPs — our infra uses dynamic ranges for shards and CDNs. we recommend: allow FQDNs in proxy passthrough with SNI preserved. If firewall requires IP ranges, allow: 3.0.0.0/8, 13.0.0.0/8, 52.0.0.0/8 (AWS ranges) *and* the customer's proxy should resolve the FQDNs themselves so SNI matches backend certs. We can provide more specific prefixes on request but model shard IPs can change.

support-customer: security won't allow wildcard CIDR open to AWS. they asked for a short-lived repro token + curl from our installer to validate which exact egress hosts we hit. can you provide a minimal command we can run in their environment to capture hosts touched by the installer?

alex: run the installer with `strace` or environment tracer to log DNS and connect syscalls, e.g.:```sudo tcpdump -ni eth0 -w /tmp/egress.pcap port 53 or port 443 &
sudo ./redwood-agent-installer --log-level debug 2>&1 | tee /tmp/installer.log
# stop tcpdump after failure and share pcap + log (scrub tokens)```

mike: alternative quick check: run `curl -v --resolve model-registry.redwood-internal:443:10.10.8.5 https://model-registry.redwood-internal/health` to force resolution and see cert returned. if cert mismatches, proxy/loadbalancer is rewriting host.

support-customer: ran `--resolve` and got same cert mismatch. they say internal LB uses cert for `registry.internal`, they can update SAN or use SNI passthrough.

sophia: final ops ask from us: please add SNI passthrough for these FQDNs and allow outbound TLS to the above list. Also allow OCSP/CRL queries to Digicert endpoints. If firewall enforce IPs, we can coordinate a test window to capture IPs and provide a short allowlist.

alex: I'll escalate to eng-infra and record the ticket. @mike can you open an internal ops runbook note about requiring SNI passthrough and the common OCSP hosts?

mike: on it. I'll create runbook and link here. For now, @support-customer please upload the pcap and installer.log to the ticket and we'll iterate. :thumbsup:
